clue.text: Academy dons mostly cramp fun

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the trimmed word wears the Academy letter inside it
mostly says the word for cramp loses its final letter

parts.note: a crick is a painful muscle spasm, a kind of cramp

explanation.surface: University dons at an academy are spoiling everyone's enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Academy dons' reads as academic staff, but 'dons' is the verb: CRIC (CRICK less its last letter, from 'mostly') puts on A.
explanation.definitionFit: Craic is an Irish word for lively fun, good company and banter.

clue.text: Restored cameo parts cut by theatre about to fail

indicators.note: restored means put back together, so these letters are reassembled
parts means the letters of cameo are taken apart and rearranged

parts.note: to crop is to cut short

indicators.note: about means the word for theatre is turned round

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: Restored cameo roles trimmed by a theatre that is about to go under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' and 'parts' both signal the anagram; 'about' turns the theatre word round. 'by' is a link word. REP is repertory theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To come a cropper is a British idiom meaning to fall heavily or fail badly.

clue.text: Did express almost derail? That's awful

indicators.note: awful means a dreadful mess, so the letters are jumbled
almost means the word derail stops just short of its end

explanation.surface: An express train nearly came off the rails: dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final L, and 'awful' scrambles DERAI. 'That's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a view is to express it, so did express is aired.

clue.text: Halved zucchinis stuffed with perhaps basil and port

indicators.note: stuffed with means the herb is packed inside the half word
halved keeps only the front half of the word for zucchinis

parts.note: zucchini is the American name for courgettes
basil is an example of a herb

explanation.surface: A recipe for zucchini halves stuffed with basil and served with port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is the harbour. Zucchinis are called courgettes in Britain, and 'Halved' keeps the front five of its ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherbourg is a major ferry and naval port in Normandy, France.

clue.text: Companion turned to catch gentleman's name

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: turned says the words for catch and gentleman are read backwards together

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
sir is the title of a gentleman or knight

explanation.surface: A companion has gone back to collect a gentleman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses both catch and gentleman together, and 'to' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To christen a ship or child is to give it a name at a ceremony.

clue.text: Poison gas inhaled by priest

indicators.note: inhaled by means taken inside the word for priest

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
Ar is the chemical symbol for argon, a gas

explanation.surface: A priest breathes in poison gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant extract that South American hunters used to poison arrows.

clue.text: Rex turned up nose at leader in Evening Echo

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: turned up means overturned, so these letters are mixed up
leader in takes the first letter of Evening

explanation.surface: King Rex snubs the editorial of a local newspaper, the Evening Echo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up nose at' looks like snubbing, but 'turned up' is the anagram signal for NOSE AT, giving ESONAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is to ring out and reverberate, as a sound echoes.

clue.text: Print extract from Mandelstam poetry

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Printing an excerpt from the poems of the Russian poet Osip Mandelstam.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp is to press a mark onto something, which is to print it.

clue.text: Severely criticise former officer, one breaking rank

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the word for rank, with the letter for one inside

parts.note: to rate is to rank or grade
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Scolding a former officer who broke ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To excoriate literally means to strip the skin, and figuratively to denounce harshly.

clue.text: Are there consumers extremely disposed to follow brand? This can tell you

indicators.note: to follow puts the rearranged letters after the word for brand

parts.note: a brand or trade mark is a mark

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so these letters are set out in a new order
extremely takes the outside letters of the word consumers

explanation.surface: A question about whether shoppers are drawn to a brand, followed by the answer: this will tell you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' signals the anagram, giving RESEARCH; 'to follow' puts it after the brand word.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveying consumers is how a firm learns whether people like its brand, so this study can tell you.

clue.text: High street houses newly let by people offering relocation

indicators.note: houses means the jumbled street holds the other letters inside
high means intoxicated, so the letters of street reel into a new order
newly means made anew, so the letters of let are rearranged

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: A high street's shops are newly rented out by people offering to move businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High street' looks like a shopping street, but 'High' signals an anagram of STREET, RESETT, which houses TLE (from 'newly let') and MEN; 'by' and 'offering' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Resettlement is moving people or things to a new place, which is relocation.

clue.text: Rock band with a real star

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rock band featuring a genuine celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock band' looks like a music genre, but 'Rock' is the anagram signal for BAND A REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red giant star in the constellation Taurus.

clue.text: Contract bridge player wears white

indicators.note: wears means the player is clothed in the word for white, so it goes inside

parts.note: pure white is spotless, untainted
South, abbreviated S, is one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A contract bridge player dressed all in white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract bridge' is the card game, but 'Contract' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To purse your lips is to draw them together, so it means to contract or pucker.

clue.text: Make good on firm promises initially after university

indicators.note: after says the first letter of promises comes behind the university letter

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
Co. is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of promises

explanation.surface: A firm making good on its promises once its graduates arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup a loss is to make it good by getting the money back.

clue.text: Punish one in scandal involving players?

indicators.note: in says the letter for one goes inside

parts.note: a scandal gets the suffix -gate after Watergate, and players in a play are the cast, so cast-gate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Should one punish someone caught up in a scandal with sports players?
explanation.walkthrough: The -gate suffix comes from Watergate and is attached to any scandal; a scandal involving a cast would be CASTGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, a way to punish.

clue.text: Kitty's backing call for strike

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for the kitty's is read in reverse

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of shared money, so kitty's gives pot's
to page someone is to call them over a speaker

explanation.surface: A pet cat being encouraged to strike out with its paw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a cat, but here it is the pot of money; 'backing' turns POTS into STOP. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt to work by employees, which is a strike.

clue.text: Locked up before Green Street festival

indicators.note: before puts the word for locked up first

parts.note: pent means shut in, as in pent-up
eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: Someone jailed just before a festival held on Green Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost, or Whitsun, is the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Plant needs a place to grow it, I answer

parts.note: a garden is a place where plants are grown

explanation.surface: A gardener explaining that a plant needs somewhere to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenia is a fragrant white-flowered shrub, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Student flat accommodates East German and Greek

indicators.note: accommodates means houses, so the flat holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A student's flat housing lodgers from East Germany and Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgrad (short for postgraduate) is a student going on to further study after a first degree.

clue.text: Batting order for cricket?

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a religious order is a sect

explanation.surface: Asking about the batting order in a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about the sport; the question mark shows cricket is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a chirping, grasshopper-like creature, an example of this kind of animal.

clue.text: Each pastry dish has cool wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping means the word for cool goes round the other piece

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent, cool
a pie is a dish baked in pastry

explanation.surface: Every pastry dish comes in a chilled wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: English detective gets court order

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: An English police detective obtains a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or order from an authority.

clue.text: Figure of speech beginning to tickle Guy?

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of tickle

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent in place

explanation.surface: A start to teasing a man called Guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative use of a word, such as a metaphor.

clue.text: Disparage, snubbing one?

indicators.note: snubbing means ignoring, so the letter for one is left out

parts.note: to depreciate something is to belittle or disparage it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A query whether to belittle someone by snubbing them.
explanation.walkthrough: DEPRECIATE and its shorter form both mean to belittle, so the whole clue both builds and defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate something is to express disapproval of it, to belittle or disparage.

clue.text: Flipping bad acting gets you animated

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: evil means bad
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in a temporary rank

explanation.surface: Really poor acting results in a lively show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse; it reverses EVIL + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alive can mean lively, full of energy, so it means animated.

clue.text: Youth gets one an unusual phone number

parts.note: a lad is a youth

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters take an odd new order

parts.note: a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: A youngster acquires a mobile with an odd phone number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phone number' looks like digits, but 'number' alone is the definition, a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: La donna è mobile is the famous tenor aria from Verdi's Rigoletto, a musical number.

clue.text: Bar's opening — first off, purchase a drink

indicators.note: opening takes the first letter of Bar's
first off means the word for purchase loses its first letter

parts.note: purchase can mean grip or leverage, a mechanical advantage

explanation.surface: As the bar opens, the first thing to do is buy a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying, but it means grip, LEVERAGE, which loses its L; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink, often used formally of tea, coffee or wine.

clue.text: Turkey lunch? That's something nice

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
to lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: A turkey lunch is a pleasant thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird; it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a special pleasure, something nice to enjoy.
